On 2024-05-18, a faint 1/10 ankle ache appeared late in a walk-jog session and resolved within 30 minutes, with no swelling, limp, instability, or focal tenderness — not a strong alarm sign, but a reason to hold rather than progress or repeat immediately. Agreed decision rule, keyed to next-morning response:
- If back to baseline the next morning: repeat the same flat walk-jog level (or slightly shorten it); don't increase speed or distance yet.
- If the ache persists, worsens, or returns with ordinary walking/stairs: take a rest day or switch to pain-free walking/cycling, stepping back from jogging.
- Only progress distance/speed after a repeat session is symptom-free both during and after.
- Seek medical evaluation for: swelling, bruising, focal bony tenderness, a limp, instability, inability to bear weight normally, increasing pain, pain at rest, or symptoms that fail to settle or keep recurring.

Why: this mirrors the conservative "wait one more cohort" style pattern the user favors elsewhere ([[feedback_stabilization_cohort]]) — don't advance on a single ambiguous data point, wait for the next check-in.
How to apply: before suggesting any increase in run distance/speed/intensity, confirm next-morning symptom status was reported as clear; if unconfirmed or symptoms recurred, recommend holding or scaling back rather than progressing.

Update 2024-05-25: symptom-free through the following week; completed a 24-min flat walk-jog (12 min of 2:1 walk:jog, then 12 min of 1:1) with no pain during or over the next 8 hours, no swelling/tenderness/limp/instability. Agreed next-week progression, one variable change at a time, each step gated on a next-morning-clear check:
1. Repeat the 24-min 2:1-then-1:1 level once more before advancing.
2. Shift ratio: same ~24–26 min, more of the session at 1:1 (e.g. 8 min 2:1, then 16–18 min 1:1).
3. Small duration increase: ~28–30 min, mostly 1:1, jog blocks capped at 1–2 min.
4. Longer jog intervals: 2 min jog : 1 min walk, same ~30 min duration.
Explicitly avoid jumping straight to 4 continuous miles — that's a later-stage goal after several clean weeks of this stepwise progression.
How to apply (update): change only one of duration or jog-ratio per step; repeat a level (don't advance) if next-morning isn't fully clear or the session felt harder than the prior one even without pain; step back to walking/cycling if ache returns during or after a session.

Update 2024-06-01: at the 30-min flat level (6 min walk, 3× [4 min jog / 2 min walk], 6 min walk cooldown), no pain during the session, but ~2 hours later a faint 1/10 outer-right-ankle ache appeared on the first few stairs and resolved within an hour; no swelling, limp, instability, bruising, or focal tenderness. This is the second ache event overall, and matches the "returns with ordinary walking/stairs" trigger — agreed to step back (rest day or pain-free walking/cycling) rather than repeat or advance, resuming flat walk-jog only after a fully clean session both during and after (including next morning). If a third ache event occurs even after backing off, that's a signal to arrange medical evaluation rather than continue self-managing.

Update 2024-06-08: after 7 symptom-free days, repeated the earlier 24-min flat walk-jog (2:1 then 1:1) rather than retrying the 30-min level that triggered the June 1 ache. No pain during or over the next 8 hours; no swelling/tenderness/limp/instability. Next-morning status not yet confirmed at time of this entry — that check is the gate before any progression. Agreed guidance: treat this as a "return to baseline after stepping back" repeat, not a new plateau to advance from — repeat the same 24-min level once more (clean during/after/next-morning) before changing anything, then move only one variable a small step (e.g. shift toward more 1:1, or jog blocks to ~2–3 min) rather than jumping to 5-min continuous jog intervals, which skips several steps of the original plan.

Update 2024-06-15: tried a flat session of three 5-min jog intervals separated by 2-min walks (plus walking warm-up/cooldown) — a notable jump past the incremental plan. No pain during the run, but ~2 hours later a mild (2/10) outer-right-ankle ache appeared and stayed noticeable for ~4 hours on stairs; still no swelling, bruising, limp, instability, focal tenderness, or rest pain. This is the third ache event overall (after 2024-05-18 and 2024-06-01), matching the pre-agreed threshold: per the 2024-06-01 entry, a third event even after backing off in between means arranging clinical evaluation rather than continuing to self-manage the progression. Recommended: hold all running, keep pain-free walking/cycling only, and see a sports medicine physician/PT/podiatrist before any further running progression — flag the delayed-onset, stairs-provoked, outer-ankle, now-recurring pattern to them.
How to apply (update): third-event threshold has now been reached — do not propose further self-directed running progressions until the user reports a clinical evaluation has occurred; only pain-free walking/cycling should be suggested in the interim.

Update 2024-06-21: no running since the 6/15 event. Ordinary walking remains pain-free with no swelling, bruising, limp, instability, or rest pain, but a single-leg hop and descending stairs now reproducibly cause a localized 2/10 outer-ankle ache. Agreed: this reinforces (not replaces) the 6/15 recommendation to get a sports-medicine/PT evaluation before resuming running — the reproducible hop/stair-descent provocation is useful detail to report to the clinician, not a reason to keep self-testing it. Interim limits: pain-free walking and low-impact cross-training (cycling, swimming) only; avoid running, jumping/hopping, and provocative stair descent; escalate beyond routine scheduling only if swelling, bruising, a limp, instability, or rest pain appear.

From [[user_book_club]] discussion, 2027-11-09: documenting previously invisible care work has a double edge. It can protect the person doing the work when credit, limits, and decision power stay with them. But increased visibility without a matching increase in shared authority makes the work easier for an institution to appropriate — the group did not treat continued invisibility as a neutral or safe default either.

This is a lens the user finds meaningful and returns to via book club discussion; it echoes a distinction they already draw at work between evidence/visibility and authority (see [[feedback_workaround_vs_institutional_evidence]], [[feedback_priya_delegation_evidence_framing]], [[feedback_ines_evidence_lock_overclaim]]) — documenting or surfacing something is not the same as it conferring standing, credit, or control to the person who did it.

Follow-up discussion, 2027-11-30: the group applied the same lens to a concrete case — a repeatedly used emergency rota. Consensus was that recording who carried that recurring coverage and its limits can expose the work without converting temporary coverage into ordinary/permanent authority. Discussion stayed literary; no Helio or household decision resulted.

User has a dog named Kibo. User does a regular ~3 mile loop on a lake trail (Lady Bird), sometimes logging conditions (weather, crowd level) as informal journal entries.

Kibo has noise/fireworks anxiety (panting, circling, avoiding windows) — confirmed 2023-07-08 during neighborhood fireworks. User's approach: low-stim interior room, brown noise, dim lights, skip walks on hot/loud pavement unless truly necessary, quick yard-only bathroom breaks if Kibo approaches the door willingly.

Kibo had a burr stuck in his paw; resolved on its own by 2023-10-09 (no limp, no swelling, stopped licking after a rinse) — no vet visit needed. Closed, not an ongoing concern.

Kibo also has storm anxiety (separate trigger from the fireworks/noise anxiety above) — confirmed as a recurring pattern, not a one-off, as of 2023-11-01 after a bad storm night. Household plan with Sam: safe under-desk spot, calming wrap, water nearby, slow post-storm walk once it passes. If Sam is working a restaurant shift during a storm, user treats covering Kibo as real household coverage (not a failed social evening) — relevant when weighing plans against Kibo needs during storms. If the reaction escalates beyond this routine, plan is to consult the vet.

Pattern recurred 2023-11-02: Kibo stayed under-desk overnight after a storm and was still notably clingy the next morning even without active crisis symptoms. Sam was out late after a restaurant shift and had another shift that same evening, so user kept the day narrower and avoided committing to late-evening work blocks. Confirms this is a genuine recurring aftercare pattern, not a single incident.

Kibo had a one-time vomiting episode (2023-12-31), attributed to grass/foam ingestion; resolved on its own — kept down water and a bland meal, normal short walk and stool, energy/gums/abdomen all normal, 6+ hours symptom-free. No vet visit needed, closed as ordinary observation, not an ongoing concern.

Kibo had a paw puncture (noted 2024-03-04); user rinsed with clean water, prevented persistent licking overnight, avoided peroxide/alcohol. Resolved by next morning — normal gait, puncture closed and dry, no swelling/warmth/discharge/fragment, Kibo stopped focusing on it. No vet visit unless symptoms recur. Closed, not an ongoing concern.

Kibo showed wariness around moving boxes (2024-03-27, tied to the [[project_holly_lease_renewal_decision]] move-out prep) — pacing, hallway-checking, avoiding usual bed, but normal appetite/water/elimination, no illness signs. This is a distinct trigger from the noise/storm anxiety above (novel-object/environmental change, not sound-based), so the brown-noise/dim-lights routine doesn't apply here — approach instead is gradual box exposure, protecting his usual quiet spot until moving day, and treating persistence/generalization beyond a few days (or any physical symptom) as the vet-call line. Resolved by 2024-03-28: moving flattened boxes behind a gate, keeping Kibo's bed/normal path clear, and letting him inspect one box at a time with treats settled him overnight — full appetite/water, acting normal the next morning. Confirms gradual box exposure works well as the go-to approach for this trigger during the rest of the Cherrywood move packing/pack-out.

New noise trigger at Cherrywood (2024-05-08): morning recycling truck caused ~8 min of barking/pacing near the front window, settled within 5 min once moved to the closed workroom with familiar blanket, water, and white noise — no panting/shaking/refusal to eat/destructive behavior after. Same underlying noise-sensitivity as the fireworks/storm anxiety above, but a new specific trigger tied to the new home's layout (street-facing window, weekly truck schedule). Plan going forward: preload white noise and move Kibo to the workroom ahead of the truck's known arrival time rather than reacting after barking starts; window covering on the trigger window as a longer-term option. Vet/behaviorist line: episodes that lengthen or intensify over repeat truck mornings instead of improving, physical symptoms outlasting the episode, destructive/self-injurious behavior, or anxiety generalizing beyond truck mornings.

On move day (5-1-24), [[user_family_mom|Mom]] took charge of Kibo entirely so the user didn't have to manage it as one more decision during the move — Riley later remarked this made the chaotic day noticeably gentler. Confirms Mom as a reliable hands-off option for Kibo coverage during high-logistics days, alongside Sam's existing storm/fireworks coverage role.

Kibo had a tick removed from behind his left ear (~7-27-24); by 8-1-24 the site was a small (~4mm) pink, slightly raised bump with a dry center — stable, non-draining, non-hot, not markedly tender, Kibo fully normal otherwise. Assessed as an ordinary local reactive bump, expected to resolve over 1-3 weeks with no intervention beyond leaving it alone/discouraging licking. No vet visit needed unless it grows, stays raised past ~3 weeks, becomes hot/swollen/draining, or systemic signs (fever, lethargy, appetite loss, lameness) appear. Closed as routine monitoring, not an ongoing concern.

Kibo has an ongoing Y-front harness fit issue: a prior medium-size harness rotated toward his armpit during use. A replacement (rated 23-29in chest; Kibo measures 25.5in) was being tested as of 2026-09-17 — two-finger clearance at neck/chest straps and clasp held under pressure, but the belly strap sat only ~1 finger-width behind the front legs vs. the fit card's ~2in recommendation, with no redness/abrasion yet. Guidance given: check whether the harness has a separate Y-front-to-belly-strap length adjuster (tightening the girth strap alone doesn't reposition it); test with 15-20 min of varied movement (turns, step-ups, front-leg reaches) rather than a calm walk, using a tape mark on the fur to catch strap migration, since the old harness's failure mode wouldn't show up in a short steady walk. If it stays: fine for outdoor use. If the strap creeps toward the armpit or clearance disappears: same failure signature as the old harness, return it.

Kibo had a shallow paw pad scrape after an evening walk (2024-11-14), with one tiny piece of gravel that rinsed out on its own; bleeding stopped, normal weight-bearing, no swelling/redness/embedded material. Same conservative pattern as the 2023 burr and 2024-03-04 puncture incidents: rinse with clean water (no peroxide/alcohol), discourage licking, skip trail walks for a day or two in favor of short soft-surface leash breaks, resume normal routine once closed. No vet visit needed absent bleeding recurrence, limping, swelling/redness, discharge, or no improvement after 2-3 days.

Storm-anxiety episode (2026-09-22, ~9pm) was more intense than the household plan's usual response: interior spot + calming wrap + water + dimmed lights only partially helped — Kibo paced/panted for ~40 min and scratched once at the closed door, while Sam was at a restaurant shift. No emergency signs (stayed responsive, drank water, pink gums, no vomiting/collapse/injury). Guidance given: layer masking sound (white/brown noise or a fan) under the wrap since that worked for his 2024-05-08 recycling-truck trigger; don't restrain the pacing, redirect with a lick mat/chew instead; keep own affect calm-flat rather than reassuring-worried; expect next-day clinginess per the 2023-11-02 pattern. This duration/intensity (40 min, door-scratching) is a step up from his baseline storm response and was flagged as worth mentioning to his regular vet as a data point (possible situational anxiety support during storm season) even though nothing tonight was urgent. Vet-call line going forward: this level of distress becoming the norm rather than occasional, door-scratching escalating into a habit risking his paws/nails, or any lingering appetite loss/limping/clinginess beyond a day or two.

Follow-through: user drafted a nonurgent email to Kibo's regular vet clinic (2025-02-02) after a second prolonged storm-anxiety episode in under two weeks (this one ~55 min of panting/pacing and repeated door-scratching, still responsive/drinking/pink gums, no emergency signs). Confirms the "worth mentioning to the vet" flag above was acted on — two escalated episodes in close succession, not a one-off, prompted the actual outreach rather than just monitoring.

Vet confirmed (2025-02-06) that the two escalated episodes above were storm anxiety and prescribed trazodone 50mg PRN: one tablet ~90 min before a forecast storm. First dose is to be given on a quiet morning (no storm) with 2 hours of observation; call the vet for marked agitation, repeated vomiting, inability to stand normally, or excessive sedation. A first-dose observation trial was planned for Saturday 2025-02-08, 9:00-11:00am, but no calendar/scheduling tool was available to actually create that event — flagging here in case the trial still needs to be scheduled or was missed.
